name: Amariah
overview: Amariah was a male Levite who served as an Aaronic priest through the lineage of Eleazar. He is identified specifically as the son of Meraioth and the father of Ahitub, situating him within the priestly family line. His role as a priest highlights his service in the religious duties established for the tribe of Levi.
namesAndTitles: The name Amariah means 'YHWH has said,' reflecting a theophoric element that underscores a connection to the Lord's declaration or authority. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 6:7, emphasizes the divine origin or approval associated with his identity.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Amariah as the son of Meraioth and the father of Ahitub, establishing a clear genealogical link within the priestly lineage. These relationships affirm his place within the Levitical family responsible for temple service.
scriptureSignificance: Amariah's significance lies in his position as an Aaronic priest descended through Eleazar, marking him as part of the sacred priesthood entrusted with worship and temple duties. His genealogy, as noted in 1 Chronicles 6:7, preserves the continuity of priestly service essential to Israel's religious life. This lineage also connects him to notable priestly descendants, reinforcing the faithfulness of God's covenant through the Levitical priesthood.
